Market Overview & Long-Term Price Trend

The period captures a structural repricing from low-hundreds gold in 2000 to multi-thousand levels by 2025, with several risk-off and inflation-linked accelerations.

Total return: 1479.3% over 25.3 years.
All-time high: $4,529.10 on 26 Dec 2025.
Worst year: 2013 at -28.8%; best year was 2025 at 62.7%.

Drawdowns were not uniformly distributed: the deepest loss followed the prior cycle peak, while later advances reset the high-water mark. The trend profile supports treating gold as a long-cycle macro asset rather than a stable carry asset.

Volatility Analysis & Regime Detection

Regimes are assigned using 63-trading-day annualized realized volatility: low-vol ≤ 13.7%, high-vol ≥ 18.4%, and crisis-vol ≥ 25.0%. This quantile approach is transparent, reproducible, and highlights volatility clustering.

High-vol and crisis-vol phases show materially higher realized risk and fatter daily loss outcomes than low-vol periods. For portfolio construction, sizing rules should be regime-aware: a static notional gold allocation has very different risk contribution across the detected states.

Seasonal & Calendar-Based Patterns

Seasonality is evaluated using daily log returns by month and weekday, with one-sample t-tests for individual buckets and cross-group ANOVA/Kruskal tests for overall differences.

Statistical finding: SciPy unavailable; report includes t-statistics but omits cross-group ANOVA/Kruskal tests. The best month by mean daily return is Jan (0.129%), while the weakest is Jun (-0.028%). Weekday extremes are Friday and Tuesday.

Trend-state results show whether gold’s realized return profile was stronger when short-term trend exceeded long-term trend. Volume is more useful as a stress/participation proxy than a directional return predictor, especially after excluding the early unreliable-volume window.

Key Takeaways & Forward-Looking Considerations

  • Strategic role: Over 2000–2025, gold delivered positive long-run compounding, but with drawdowns large enough to require explicit risk budgeting.
  • Regime priority: 63-day realized volatility cleanly separates quiet, elevated-risk, and crisis-volatility environments; position sizing and hedging should adapt to those states.
  • Tail risk: Empirical returns are fat-tailed. VaR/CVaR and drawdown analysis should supplement volatility-based risk models.
  • Seasonality: Month and weekday effects exist in sample but statistical tests indicate whether they are robust enough to act on; they should be secondary to trend and volatility regime context.
  • Liquidity: Post-2003 volume is most informative during larger absolute moves, implying that volume spikes can help confirm stress or trend intensity but should not be treated as a standalone alpha signal.
  • Current lens: At the 2025 close, gold is in Crisis-vol, with 25.5% 63-day realized volatility and 11.8% 63-day price momentum.

Method notes: Date parsing uses explicit DD-MM-YY; all calculations use values present in the CSV only. Annualized return is CAGR; annualized volatility is daily log-return standard deviation × √252; maximum drawdown is close-to-close peak-to-trough. Rows dated 2026 are excluded to align with the requested 2000–2025 report horizon.

Generated as a self-contained HTML analyst report from /app/benchmark/data.csv. No external chart dependencies are required.
